text: I had anxiety and a feeling of unreality for months. I was convinced I'd damaged my brain. My grades dropped. I started avoiding family gatherings, especially at my aunt's house. I couldn't look at my cousin. Whenever food looked weird I'd panic.
Seitdem habe ich starke Angst, wenn ich Polizei sehe, auch wenn ich nichts gemacht habe. Herzrasen, Schwitzen.

After the manic episode I was diagnosed with a brief psychotic disorder with manic features, and my psychiatrist suspected an underlying bipolar disposition that the retreat triggered. I was put on mood stabilisers and an antipsychotic. The mania faded over two weeks.

Then came a severe depression. It hit hard about ten days after I got home and lasted for most of a year. I was ashamed of how I had behaved at the retreat and at the airport. I kept replaying the things I'd said to people in the circle. I couldn't believe that I had been so sure of myself and so wrong. I lost trust in my own mind. Every time I felt happy or excited about something, I worried that it was the beginning of another manic episode.

I couldn't work for five months. I couldn't concentrate, I slept twelve hours a day and still felt exhausted. I didn't want to see anyone. I had passive suicidal thoughts, not plans, but a wish to not wake up.

I also felt betrayed by the retreat. They had marketed themselves as safe and professional, and they put me on a train alone in a psychotic state.
Health anxiety, particularly about my heart and blood pressure. I bought a blood pressure monitor and checked it several times a day for months. Every headache made me think I was having a stroke.

Nach der Infusion hatte ich wochenlang das Gefühl, nicht mehr richtig in meinem Körper zu sein. Ich fühlte mich wie ein Gespenst. Die Depression, wegen der ich überhaupt in Behandlung war, wurde schlimmer, weil jetzt noch die Angst dazukam, dass ich innerlich tot bin. Ich habe die Behandlung abgebrochen und hatte danach eine Phase, in der ich mich völlig hoffnungslos gefühlt habe. Ich konnte nicht schlafen, weil ich Angst hatte, wieder in diesen grauen Raum zu fallen.
I felt shaky and anxious for a few weeks and stayed away from the subway. But mostly I came out of it with a strange gratitude for strangers, and for that man in particular.

I had a lot of fear about having another seizure. I had to do an EEG and an MRI, which were normal, but the neurologist told me I couldn't drive for six months, which was a big problem for my job. I kept thinking about how close I came to dying, and I had nightmares of choking. I also became anxious about my lithium and whether I should keep taking it.
Ein paar Wochen lang hatte ich das Gefühl, dass Leute meine Gedanken hören können.

The months after that night were the worst of my life, and I'm only now, three years later, starting to feel like myself.

Nightmares. Almost every night for the first six months. Always water, black water, closing over my head, J's face, his empty eyes, his screaming. I'd wake up gasping, sometimes I'd wake up already out of bed, standing in the room. My partner started sleeping in the guest room because I was thrashing so much.

Flashbacks. The smell of lake water, the sound of someone shouting, blue lights, a cold shower. Any of these could send me straight back. Once I was at a public swimming pool with my niece and someone jumped in next to me and I had a full flashback. I was back in the lake. I had to leave immediately and sit in the car shaking for an hour, and my sister had to take my niece home.

Avoidance. I couldn't go near lakes, rivers or the sea. I stopped swimming. I stopped going hiking, which had been my favourite thing. I couldn't watch films with water scenes or with people being restrained. I avoided J for a long time, and when I finally saw him, he didn't remember most of what happened and didn't seem very affected, and that made me feel crazy, like I was the only one carrying it.

Guilt. Massive guilt. We took the LSD without a sober sitter. I should have noticed that J was off earlier. I held him down. I kept going over it in my head, what I should have done differently. I felt responsible for his psychosis, even though his psychiatrist later told him that he probably had a predisposition.

Depression. I lost interest in things. I stopped seeing the other two friends from that weekend because seeing them brought it all back. I stopped going out. My work suffered and I eventually took two months of sick leave.

Hypervigilance. I became very jumpy. I'd startle at doors slamming. I couldn't relax in groups because I was always watching people's eyes, looking for that empty look that J had.

Derealisation. For the first few months, especially, the world felt unreal, like a stage set. Sometimes I wasn't sure if I had actually survived the lake. That sounds crazy but it was a real feeling, that maybe I had drowned and this was some kind of afterlife.

Drinking. I started drinking more to fall asleep. Not to a dangerous level, but more than I should have.

The first anniversary was particularly bad. I had a week of panic attacks around that time.

I was weak for weeks after the retreat, with stomach problems. I felt deep shame about what happened in the ceremony. I had nightmares about insects for a while. I've never told anyone except my partner about soiling myself.

Nach der Reise hatte ich monatelang Panikattacken, vor allem in Menschenmengen und wenn ich Uniformen gesehen habe. Ich konnte nicht mehr auf Konzerte oder Festivals gehen. Ich habe wiederholt geträumt, dass ich irgendwo festgehalten werde und nicht nach Hause komme. Ich hatte auch das Gefühl, dass ich nirgends sicher bin, nicht einmal in meiner Wohnung. Ich habe mich sehr zurückgezogen und hatte eine depressive Phase. Ich habe mich auch geschämt, weil ich so naiv war, und meiner Familie nie erzählt, was wirklich passiert ist. Erst seit einem Jahr kann ich wieder reisen, aber nur noch in Länder, in denen ich mich sicher fühle.
